shared_elements: row of three arched/loop-shaped motifs along the upper register
small animal figures perched on or above the arched motifs
horizontal band with vertical hatching / fringe-like strokes running across the surface
bird-like creature in profile with long neck and beak
circular disc held or placed beside a figure
low-relief carving on a flat rectangular stone face
justification: Both surfaces repeat a very specific compositional scheme: three arched, bag-like motifs in a row across the top, each with a small animal above, a hatched/fringed horizontal band immediately beneath them, and profile bird- and snake-like creatures with a disc in the register below — the shallow, flat-planed relief with incised contour lines looks like the same carving manner. The main differences are that B is an isolated, more heavily pitted slab that continues into a further lower register with a large winged/quadruped figure, while A is shown in situ and abraded, with its lower animals arranged and detailed somewhat differently.
